title: autocalibrated-canary-prober: self-tuning canary probing and baseline drift compensation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces an autonomously calibrated canary prober that adapts probe frequency and detection sensitivity to live traffic fingerprints and baseline volatility. Improves canary signal stability and reduces false positives during traffic shape shifts.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a self-tuning 'autocalibrated canary prober' service and accompanying rollout-guard logic to make continuous performance canaries more robust to baseline drift and traffic-shape changes. Motivation: current canary detectors are brittle when traffic seasonality or sudden shift in request mix changes baseline latency/throughput distributions. That results in noise-driven rollbacks or missed regressions. The prober autonomously calibrates probe rates and detector sensitivity based on observed volatility and a compact traffic fingerprint, enabling stable canary decisions without manual parameter tuning.

Design and changes: 1) new service redwood/canary/prober that maintains a rolling multi-scale baseline (quantiles + EWMA volatility) per route and region, and computes a probe schedule using a Bayesian calibration step that trades probe overhead vs. detection confidence; 2) hierarchical detectors: short-window rapid detector for large regressions, and long-window drift detector with decay-aware baselines for gradual regressions; 3) confidence scoring & backoff: detection events surface a confidence score used by rollout-guard policies to decide immediate rollback, staged pause, or monitored continue; 4) probe shaping via traffic fingerprint: gentle probing preserves production traffic mix by sampling user-agent and request-size strata and adaptively targeting underrepresented slices; 5) transparent metrics: new tracing tags and metrics (canary.prober.*) for per-probe latency, probe-overhead, baseline-delta, confidence_score, and decision_reason; 6) integrations: hooks in perf-canary pipeline, canary UI flags in Console, and an operator-facing CLI for dry-run calibration.

Files & modules touched (high level): redwood/canary/prober/{service,calibrator,detectors}.go, redwood/observability/metrics_registry.go (new metrics + dashboards), redwood/perf-canary/runner.go (integration), redwood/rollouts/guard_manager.go (policy logic), infra/helm/canary-values.yaml (feature flagging), docs/perf-canary/autocal-prober.md.

Testing: unit tests cover calibrator priors, synthetic workload simulations and edge cases (zero traffic, extreme skew). Integration tests executed in perf-canary pipeline include: (a) controlled regression injection (10–30% tokenization overhead) to validate rapid detector; (b) gradual drift (0.5–2% per minute) to validate long-window stabilization; (c) traffic-shape change tests where request-size distribution shifts to ensure probe stratification avoids blind spots. Canary e2e run was performed as shadow traffic on a small subset of clusters.

Deployment & rollout: feature-flag gated. Rollout plan: shadow mode (0% impact) in perf-canary pipeline -> shadowed live probes on 0.2% of traffic for 24h -> staged rollout to 2% with automated monitoring -> full enablement behind operator approval. New alerts created for canary.prober.confidence_score drop and probe-overhead > 1.5x expected.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc: ENG-2041 link in Linear
- [x] unit tests added
- [x] integration tests in perf-canary pipeline
- [x] dashboards and alerts added
- [x] docs/perf-canary/autocal-prober.md

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps default calibration conservative (low probe footprint, higher detection thresholds) to avoid spurious rollbacks during initial rollout. Operators can tune priors via the CLI or Helm values. Related work: builds on the traffic-fingerprinting ideas from ENG-1723 and complements the rollout-guard framework implemented in ENG-2107. For troubleshooting, set CANARY_PROBER_DEBUG=1 to emit detailed probe traces to tracing.

review_conversation: Luca Ortega (reviewer): This looks promising; question on calibrator priors — what prevents oscillation when traffic flips rapidly?

Maya Chen (author): Calibrator uses an EWMA volatility term and a shrinkage prior keyed by route fingerprint; when volatility spikes we back off probe aggressiveness and increase aggregation window to avoid oscillation.
Priya Nair (reviewer): CI integration uses synthetic load; can we add a smoke test that simulates sudden endpoint cold-starts?
Maya Chen (author): Added a smoke scenario in perf-canary integration that injects cold-start latency and validated detector behavior; test added in commit b98f6d1.
Samir Patel (reviewer): lgtm after a couple nits on metric names and a doc clarification.
merge_notes: Merged after addressing test additions and metric renames. CI initially failed on a flaky e2e; rerun passed. No manual rollback required during shadow run.
notes_for_ops: Default config is conservative; to speed detection reduce canary.prober.prior_conservatism via CLI.
If you see continuous low-confidence detections, enable debug traces and inspect canary.prober.baseline_delta histogram.
